title: Care situation of knee ligament instability as a registry study.
summary: The aim of this registry is to evaluate the clinical outcome of patients after surgical treatment of ligamentous instability compared to patients with conservative therapy of ligamentous instability (primary endpoint re-instability). In a second study arm (secondary endpoint), potential reasons for re-failure or insufficient improvement of clinical outcome (based on clinical scores and instrumental measurement) such as leg axis deformities, meniscal lesions, ligamentous concomitant instabilities or insufficient strengthening of the muscles surrounding the knee, etc. will be evaluated. Clinical outcomes include subjective functional parameters (IKDC, Lysholm, Tegner) as well as objective stability parameters such as an instrumental measurement (e.g. Rolimeter) or pivot shift and Lachman. In order to record patients even without surgical therapy and to follow them up in the long term, it is only possible to perform this study in the context of a registry.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- All patients (>18 years) who were or will be treated at BG Klinikum Hamburg in the above-mentioned period due to a mishealed ligament instability will be included. 
- Presence of a ligament injury of the knee joint requiring treatment (conservative or surgical).
- Presence of a signed declaration of consent for the scientific evaluation of patient data assigned to the treatment in question.
- Patients with pre-existing joint wear disease of the injured knee joint at the time of inclusion
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients who do not have an independently signed consent for data use (e.g., signature by relatives due to impaired cognitive function, as an exception, signatures of others as a witness function in the case of impaired hand function).
- Patients with impaired cognitive function which does not allow the nature of this registry study to be conveyed.
- Patients with multiple lower extremity injuries or polytrauma.
- Patients with previous ligament injuries of the affected knee joint as far as NO details about the treatment method are known.
